cands.name: Jeffrey C. McNeely
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 84 (Iredell County) since July 2019, when he was appointed to fill Rena Turner's seat. Manages his family's business, G & M Milling Co. Former Iredell County commissioner (elected 2016) and longtime Iredell County Planning Board member.

controversies.text: In May 2023, during a House debate, McNeely asked Rep. Abe Jones, who is Black, whether he could have gotten into Harvard if he were not "an athlete or a minority." McNeely apologized, calling it a "misstep," and Jones accepted. McNeely then resigned as deputy whip after GOP leaders sought it. He kept his seat.

endorsements.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey McNeely listed endorsements from Speaker Tim Moore, the State Employees Association and the NC Farm Bureau. This is self-reported, and Ballotpedia did not independently identify any endorsements.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position from McNeely on data centers or on development projects. We found no documented actions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. His one stated tax position is "Lower State Taxes" in a 2024 survey, which does not specify homestead taxes. The detail of the 2023 remarks that led to his deputy whip resignation was not available. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and no endorsements were independently identified. His Ballotpedia sponsored-legislation list did not load, so no bills he sponsored could be confirmed.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Statesville, NC, and his campaign site says he is a lifelong Iredell County resident who attended West Iredell High School and returned there after NC State.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2019; Iredell County commissioner from 2016 to 2020; Iredell County Planning Board member for about 16 years, three as chair; manager of the family business G & M Milling Co.; B.S. in Agricultural Economics from NC State.
qual.why: He has several years of state legislative service, including a seat on the House Appropriations Committee, and earlier local elected office. He also has a business management background. Committee chair posts were not counted.
